Artificial Intelligence is the field of computer science focused on building machines that can perform tasks that normally require human intelligence, like reasoning, learning, and decision-making.
AI works by training systems on large amounts of data so they can recognize patterns, make predictions, or take actions — similar to how humans learn from experience.

Artificial Intelligence refers to systems that simulate human cognitive functions. Techniques like machine learning, deep learning, and NLP allow AI to learn, understand language, and make smart decisions.
Machine Learning is a subset of AI where systems learn from data rather than being explicitly programmed. The algorithm finds patterns and improves its performance with more data over time.

ML works by feeding an algorithm labeled data, letting it find patterns, and then using those patterns to make predictions on new data. Examples include spam filters, recommendation engines, and image recognition.
Machine Learning is teaching a computer to make decisions by showing it many examples. It is the core technology behind Netflix recommendations, fraud detection, and voice assistants.
Deep Learning is a type of machine learning that uses multi-layered neural networks to learn from large amounts of data. It powers image recognition, speech-to-text, and language models.
Neural networks in deep learning are inspired by the human brain. They have layers of nodes that process data, and with enough data, they can learn very complex patterns.
Deep Learning uses deep neural networks with many hidden layers to learn features automatically from raw data like images, audio, or text — making it the foundation of modern AI systems.

CORS stands for Cross-Origin Resource Sharing. It is a browser security mechanism that controls which websites can make requests to your backend API from different domains.
When your frontend is on one domain and backend on another, the browser blocks requests by default for security. CORS headers tell the browser it is safe to allow those requests.
Deepak's FastAPI backend uses CORS middleware to allow his portfolio frontend at deepak-l.me to call the AI API backend without being blocked by browser security policies.
JSON stands for JavaScript Object Notation. It is a lightweight text format for storing and exchanging data, widely used for API responses and configuration files.
JSON uses key-value pairs and is easy for both humans to read and machines to parse. Deepak's AI assistant stores all profile data in a profile.json file that the backend reads.
JSON is the standard format for data exchange between a frontend and backend. When Deepak's chatbot sends your question and gets an answer, the data travels as JSON.

Middleware is code that runs between receiving a request and sending a response. In Deepak's FastAPI backend, CORS middleware intercepts every request to add the right headers for cross-origin access.
Middleware acts like a checkpoint in your server. It can check authentication, add headers, log requests, or modify data before your main function handles the request.
FastAPI uses middleware like CORS to process every incoming request before it reaches your route handler. It is a clean way to apply cross-cutting logic across all endpoints.
